text.p: Standard Chartered Plc, the London-based bank which has its principle franchise in Asia, is expected to post a healthy rise in 1996 pretax profits when it reports next Wednesday.
Forecasts for pretax profit centre around the 860 to 870 million stg mark after 661 million in 1995 and analysts see a dividend payment for the year of some 14 to 15p per share after 11p.

At the half-way stage, StanChart tried to temper market exuberance by warning that it expected to see slower growth in mortgage lending and analysts also expect profits to be hit by the firm pound and dull foreign exchange markets in 1996.

This has led some analysts to trim their expectations but most remain bullish on StanChart shares, which have put in an excellent market performance over the past two years, sometimes boosted by takeover talk, which has recently subsided.
Analysts expect some rise in costs for 1996, with the focus switching from the restructuring seen in recent years to growth in the business.
But cost income ratio will fall, with a healthy rise in revenue easily outstripping the cost rise.
The revenue rise is seen coming from the bank's large commercial banking activities and, to a lesser extent, from its corporate book.
Non-interest income is likely to have been more problematical with the loss of the contribution from the private banking unit sold last year and sluggish foreign exchange revenue.
Provisions against bad debts are likely to be higher but this will be a function of volume, especially in credit cards, rather than a lowering of quality.

Analysts see little chance of StanChart returning capital to shareholders, other than in dividend payments, despite the fact that its tier one capital ratio is likely to be comfortably over eight percent.
They say the bank is likely to continue to utilise capital to expand its Asian franchise in the next few years.
